hints: Think about what has just finished before G2 starts. What happened to the DNA during the S phase?
Picture one duplicated chromosome in late G2. How many sister chromatids (and so how many DNA molecules) does it have, and how many centromeres hold them together?
walkthrough:
**Recall the order of interphase**

Interphase goes $G_1$ then S then $G_2$. DNA replication happens in S phase, so by the end of $G_2$ every chromosome has already been copied.

Think: one chromosome in, two copies out.

**Picture a chromosome at the end of G2**

After replication, each chromosome consists of two identical sister chromatids joined together. Each sister chromatid contains one complete DNA molecule.

So: 1 chromosome = 2 chromatids = 2 molecules of DNA.

**Check the other structures**

The two chromatids are held together at a single shared centromere region. Centrioles are separate cytoplasmic structures, not part of the chromosome. Each chromatid also has a telomere at each end, so there are four telomeres in total, not two.

options.A: Centrioles are in the centrosome in the cytoplasm and organise the spindle. They are never part of a chromosome.
options.B: The two sister chromatids share one common centromere region that holds them together, so there is only one centromere per chromosome.
options.C: DNA was replicated in S phase, so each chromosome at the end of G2 has two sister chromatids, each with one DNA molecule.
options.D: Each chromatid has two ends and so two telomeres. A duplicated chromosome with two chromatids therefore has four telomeres.
